title: Redis Data Store
description: Redis reference covering data types, expiration, caching, transactions, Lua/functions, streams, Pub/Sub, persistence, replication, clustering, security, observability, and failure-safe production use.

subtopics.title: Strings, Hashes, Lists, Sets, Sorted Sets & Streams
subtopics.description: Choose a native type by operations, not serialized shape; Redis commands are atomic individually but compound workflows need explicit coordination.

codeBlocks.code:
SET session:abc '{"userId":42}' EX 1800 NX
HSET user:42 name Ada plan pro
ZADD leaderboard 1500 user:42
XRANGE orders - + COUNT 10

subtopics.title: Key Design, TTL & Memory
subtopics.description: Namespace keys consistently, keep them bounded, set TTL at creation, and choose eviction policy from data-loss semantics.

codeBlocks.code:
SET cache:user:42 <value> EX 300
TTL cache:user:42
MEMORY USAGE cache:user:42
SCAN 0 MATCH cache:user:* COUNT 100

callouts.title: Never Use KEYS in Production Paths
callouts.text: KEYS scans the full keyspace synchronously. Use SCAN for operations and maintain explicit indexes for application queries.

subtopics.title: Redis 8 Query, JSON, Time Series & Vectors
subtopics.description: Redis 8 integrates capabilities formerly shipped separately, including JSON documents, time series, probabilistic structures, full-text/query indexing, and vector search. Redis 8.8 also adds arrays and a native window-counter rate limiter.

codeBlocks.code:
Choose by access pattern:
JSON + secondary indexes → queryable document fields
Time series → timestamped measurements and server aggregation
Bloom/Cuckoo filters → probabilistic membership
Vector indexes/sets → similarity search
Array → sparse or dense index-addressed string values

callouts.title: Indexing Changes the Cost Model
callouts.text: Integrated query features consume memory and write CPU. Define index scope, vector precision, retention, consistency, and failure behavior before treating Redis as a general system of record.

subtopics.title: Cache-Aside, Write-Through & Stampede Control
subtopics.description: Cache-aside loads on miss and invalidates after authoritative writes. Use TTL jitter, request coalescing, and stale serving to prevent stampedes.

codeBlocks.code:
read: cache GET -> miss -> DB read -> SET value EX ttl+jitter
write: DB transaction commit -> invalidate cache key
never treat cache as authoritative unless persistence/failure model supports it

callouts.title: Invalidation Follows the Source-of-Truth Commit
callouts.text: Invalidating before a failed database write can repopulate stale data; updating cache without database commit can publish nonexistent state.

subtopics.title: WATCH/MULTI, Lua & Locks
subtopics.description: MULTI/EXEC queues commands; WATCH adds optimistic concurrency; Lua/functions atomically execute server-side logic. Distributed locks require ownership tokens and bounded validity.

codeBlocks.code:
SET lock:job:42 <random-token> NX PX 30000
# release atomically only when stored token equals caller token

callouts.title: A Redis Lock Is a Lease, Not a Proof of Completion
callouts.text: Account for pauses, expiry, failover, retries, fencing tokens, and idempotent operations before protecting critical external side effects.

subtopics.title: Pub/Sub vs Streams
subtopics.description: Pub/Sub is ephemeral fan-out to currently connected subscribers; Streams persist entries and support consumer groups, acknowledgements, and pending recovery.

subtopics.title: Consumer Groups & Recovery
subtopics.description: Acknowledge only after side effects commit, inspect pending entries, reclaim abandoned work, trim deliberately, and make consumers idempotent.

codeBlocks.code:
XGROUP CREATE orders workers $ MKSTREAM
XREADGROUP GROUP workers worker-1 COUNT 10 BLOCK 5000 STREAMS orders >
XACK orders workers 1710000000000-0
XPENDING orders workers

subtopics.title: RDB, AOF, Replication & Cluster
subtopics.description: RDB provides snapshots; AOF logs writes; replicas improve reads/failover but replication is asynchronous; Cluster shards hash slots and constrains multi-key operations.

callouts.title: Replication Is Not Backup
callouts.text: Accidental deletes and corrupt writes replicate. Keep independent tested backups and understand acknowledged-write loss during failover.

subtopics.title: Security, Observability & Checklist
subtopics.description: Use private networking, TLS/auth/ACLs, command restrictions, latency and memory monitoring, slow logs, capacity alarms, and restore/failover drills.

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Bound keys and values, set TTLs, avoid KEYS, select eviction policy, make consumers idempotent, protect hot keys, monitor latency/memory/evictions, back up, and rehearse failover.
